newsitem.title: FINLAND: Nokia, softer dollar seen taking Helsinki lower.
newsitem.headline: Nokia, softer dollar seen taking Helsinki lower.

text.p: Shares were seen opening lower on Monday, with the softer dollar likely to weigh on dollar-sensitive stocks, and Nokia was seen opening down to match its Wall Street close last Friday, brokers said.
"I expect the weaker dollar to have an impact on cyclicals today," one broker said, adding, that volumes were usually thin on Mondays.

Nokia ended flat at around 323.56 markka in New York, but well down compared to its 329.50 markka Helsinki close. "Nokia will match its New York close and fall some five markka at the opening," another broker said.
Brokers said forestry shares in particular could be hurt by the weaker dollar and the sector index was seen dragged lower by losses in U.S. paper stocks last Friday.
Forestry group Metsa-Serla's Q1 earnings report is due out today at around 1200/0900 GMT.
Europe's biggest forestry group UPM-Kymmene reports first-quarter earnings on Tuesday at 0800/0500 GMT.
